Problem_Classification.Domain: Monte Carlo Simulation / Discrete Choice Modeling (Econometrics / Statistics)
Problem_Classification.Algorithm: Simulated Multinomial Probit Choice Probabilities (argmax-of-utilities Monte Carlo estimator)
Problem_Classification.Algorithm_Purpose: For each of n observations, estimate the probability that each of K alternatives yields the maximum latent utility W_k = alpha_{i,k} + epsilon_k (epsilon ~ N(0,1)), by simulating M draws and counting argmax frequencies. Output is an n×K matrix of choice probabilities.
Problem_Classification.Algorithm_Steps: 1. Host reads n×K alpha matrix from CSV; generates M×K standard-normal draws with std::mt19937. 2. Host transfers alphas and rands to device (and transposed versions for kernels 2/3). 3. Each GPU thread is assigned one observation i (row). 4. The thread loops m = 0..M-1: forms K utilities w[k] = alpha[i,k] + rand[m,k] in a local register array w[21]. 5. Performs a linear scan over k to find argmax of w. 6. Increments the per-row counter probs[i, argmax] by 1. 7. After M iterations, divides each of K counters by M to get probabilities. 8. Three kernel variants: (1) row-major naive, (2) transposed for coalesced loads, (3) transposed + shared-memory staging of w[] and probs[]. 9. Host verifies against a serial CPU reference and reports timing.
Problem_Classification.Reference_Complexity: Time: O(n · M · K) arithmetic operations ≈ 26,280 · 10,000 · 21 ≈ 5.52 × 10^9 inner-loop ops. Space: O(n·K + M·K) — alphas + probs (n·K doubles each) and rands (M·K doubles); per-thread local w[K] in registers; for kernel 3 an additional 2·K·blockDim shared-memory tile.

Bottleneck_Analysis.Classification: Compute-bound (FP64-throughput limited on GA102); secondarily latency/occupancy-limited for the shared-memory variant.
Bottleneck_Analysis.Arithmetic_Intensity: Per row i: ~M·(2K) ≈ 10,000·42 ≈ 4.2×10^5 FP64 ops (K adds + K-1 compares + 1 increment per MC draw). Unique bytes touched per row (cache-resident view): K alphas (168 B) + M·K rands (1.68 MB, shared across all rows) + K probs writes (168 B). Total problem FLOPs: n·M·2K ≈ 1.1 × 10^10. Total unique device-memory footprint: alphas (4.21 MB) + rands (1.60 MB) + probs (4.21 MB) ≈ 10 MB, entirely L2-resident on the 6 MB L2 after warm-up of rands/probs. AI (assuming rands stays L2-resident across the n-thread grid): ≈ 1.1×10^10 / 1.0×10^7 ≈ 1.1 × 10^3 FLOP/Byte. AI (cold/no-reuse pessimistic view, counting every rand re-fetch through DRAM): ≈ 1.1×10^10 / (n·M·K·8 B) ≈ 1.1×10^10 / 4.4×10^10 ≈ 0.25 FLOP/Byte.
Bottleneck_Analysis.Ridge_Point_Comparison: RTX A6000 FP64 peak ≈ 84 SMs · 2 FP64 ops/cycle · 2 (FMA) · 1.8 GHz ≈ 0.6 TFLOPS FP64; peak DRAM BW ≈ 768 GB/s. Ridge point ≈ 0.6×10^12 / 7.68×10^11 ≈ 0.78 FP64-FLOP/Byte. Realistic AI (≈1.1×10^3) is well ABOVE the ridge point ⇒ workload sits in the compute-bound regime once rands is L2-resident.
Bottleneck_Analysis.Dominant_Limiter: FP64 ALU throughput on consumer-class Ampere (GA102 has only 2 FP64 cores per SM, i.e. 1/64 of FP32). Secondary limiters: warp divergence in the argmax linear scan, and (for kernel 3) bank conflicts / occupancy drop from a 32 KB shared-memory footprint per 96-thread block.

Memory_Access_Profile.Pattern: Kernel 1 (compute_probs): row-major layout alphas[i·K+k], probs[i·K+k] — strided-by-K across the warp ⇒ uncoalesced 32-way gathers. Kernels 2 & 3 (unitStrides): transposed layout alphas[k·n+i], probs[k·n+i] — unit stride across threads in the warp ⇒ fully coalesced streaming. rands access: kernel 1 reads rands[m·K+k] (broadcast across warp, same m and k per cycle ⇒ already broadcastable); kernels 2/3 read rands[k·M+m] (also broadcast across the warp). Overall: streaming + broadcast, with the entire rands buffer (1.6 MB) hot in L2 / read-only cache.
Memory_Access_Profile.Read_Write_Ratio: Per row: M·K + K reads (≈ 2.10×10^5 doubles) vs. M increments + K finalization writes (≈ 1.00×10^4 doubles to global in kernels 1/2; only K=21 global writes in kernel 3 because the M increments hit shared memory). Effective ratio: ≈ 21:1 (kernels 1/2) and ≈ 10,000:1 (kernel 3, global only). Algorithm-level read:write ≈ 21:1.
Memory_Access_Profile.Reuse_Factor: alphas[i,k]: read M = 10,000 times by the owning thread (kept in register w[k] inside one MC step but re-loaded each m in this code). rands[m,k]: read n = 26,280 times across the grid (huge reuse — fits in L2 / read-only cache, ideal for __constant__ or texture caching if it were smaller). probs[i,k]: updated M times in kernels 1/2 (global RMW), reduced to K writes in kernel 3 via shared memory.
Memory_Access_Profile.Coalescing_Feasibility: Kernel 1: poor — requires transformation. Kernels 2/3: natural coalescing achieved by host-side transpose of alphas (n×K → K×n) and rands (M×K → K×M).
Memory_Access_Profile.Optimal_Tiling_Hint: (a) Transpose layouts to K-major so threads in a warp index along n (already done in kernels 2/3). (b) Stage rands in shared memory or rely on the read-only / L2 cache — rands is only 1.60 MB and is reused n times. (c) Stage per-thread w[] and the K probability counters in shared memory to remove repeated global RMWs (kernel 3 pattern). Size: 2·K·blockDim·8 B; for blockDim=96, K=21 ⇒ 32,256 B/block — fits in 100 KB/SM but caps occupancy to ≈3 blocks/SM = 288 threads/SM. (d) Better: keep w[] in registers (it already is via the local array w[21]) and only stage the K-entry probability counter in shared memory (or even registers as 21 scalars), dropping shared-mem usage to ~21·blockDim·8 B = 16 KB at blockDim=96, allowing higher occupancy. (e) For very high-K work, tile the K dimension so the per-thread argmax scan stays in registers and uses warp shuffles.

Parallelism_Structure.Granularity: One thread per observation i (one row of the n×K probability matrix). Each thread performs M·(K adds + K-1 compares + 1 write) ≈ 4.2×10^5 ops independently.
Parallelism_Structure.Independence: Fully independent across rows — no inter-thread data dependency. Within a thread the M Monte Carlo iterations are also independent (could be parallelised further across threads if desired).
Parallelism_Structure.Synchronization: None. No __syncthreads(), no atomics, no warp primitives. Kernel 3 uses shared memory only as per-thread private scratch (each thread owns column threadIdx.x of the shared tile) so no sync is required there either.
Parallelism_Structure.Recommended_Block_Size: For kernels 1/2 (register-only, no shared memory): on cc 8.6 with 1536 threads/SM and 65,536 regs/SM, 128–256 threads/block hits full 1536-thread occupancy. The code's choice of 192 yields exactly 8 blocks = 1536 threads/SM and is near-optimal. For kernel 3 (32 KB shared/block at blockDim=96): occupancy is shared-memory-limited to ~3 blocks/SM = 288 threads/SM, so 96 is a deliberate trade-off; reducing the shared footprint (e.g. dropping the shared w[] and using registers) would allow 128–256 threads/block with full occupancy.

Hardware_Constraints.Shared_Memory_Per_Block: 99 KB (101,376 B) opt-in dynamic; 48 KB default
Hardware_Constraints.GPU_Clock_Rate: Max SM clock 2100 MHz (typical sustained boost ≈ 1800 MHz); max memory clock 8001 MHz

Data_Shape.Input_Dimensions: n = 26,280 observations; K = 21 alternatives; M = 10,000 Monte Carlo draws. alphas: 26,280 × 21. rands: 10,000 × 21. probs: 26,280 × 21.
Data_Shape.Data_Type: float64 (double, IEEE-754 binary64) throughout — kernels declare double w[21]; division by M_d is FP64.
Data_Shape.Total_Memory_Footprint: Device: alphas 4,415,040 B + rands 1,680,000 B + probs 4,415,040 B ≈ 10,510,080 B ≈ 10.03 MB. Host: same three buffers + probs_ref (4.21 MB) + transposed t_alphas (4.21 MB) + t_rands (1.60 MB) ≈ 20.05 MB. Per-thread local: w[21] = 168 B in registers (21 doubles). Kernel 3 shared memory per block: 2 · K · blockDim · 8 B = 2 · 21 · 96 · 8 = 32,256 B.
